courses.name: Asheville Municipal Golf Course
courses.summary: Donald Ross's 1927 municipal gem — the first racially integrated golf course in North Carolina and a National Register property. Currently playing back nine twice while the Helene-damaged front nine is restored.
courses.insider_tip: Add one full club on every approach — the back nine plays consistently uphill coming in.

courses.name: Broadmoor Golf Links
courses.summary: WNC's only true links-style layout, redesigned by Karl Litten (PGA's 'Fab Four'). Post-Helene redesign reopened May 2026 — discard old yardage books, the routing has shifted.
courses.insider_tip: Play the course fresh — prior yardage books are obsolete after the May 2026 redesign.

courses.name: Reems Creek Golf Club
courses.summary: Designed by Hawtree & Sons — architects of Royal Birkdale — the only WNC course built by an active Open Championship rota firm. Pot bunkers, fescue rough, and Scottish Highland character throughout.
courses.insider_tip: Carry an extra club on holes 14–16. The upvalley wind is consistently underestimated.

courses.name: Chestnut Mountain Golf Club
courses.summary: Tom Jackson's 1976 design inside the gated High Vista community — 350+ feet of vertical change across 18 holes, among the most dramatic relief of any public course in Buncombe County.
courses.insider_tip: The par-4 4th (324 yards) is a trap — the green rejects anything missing right by more than five feet.

courses.name: Lake Junaluska Golf Course
courses.summary: Opened 1919 on a United Methodist conference center — one of WNC's oldest active layouts. Plays harder than the slope suggests; small, sloped greens punish imprecise irons.
courses.insider_tip: Favor the middle of every green on the lake-adjacent back nine holes — the westerly breeze kills distance.

courses.name: Sherwood Forest Golf Club
courses.summary: Affordable, no-frills Henderson County local favorite. Rolling terrain, tree-lined fairways, bentgrass greens. Call ahead — online info is inconsistently maintained.
courses.insider_tip: Always call before visiting — hours and conditions change seasonally without notice.

courses.name: Connestee Falls Golf Club
courses.summary: George W. Cobb 1972 design — same architect as Augusta's Par-3 Course. Multiple creek crossings, natural terrain hazards. Outside access limited to non-peak morning slots.
courses.insider_tip: Book direct through the pro shop — weekend member times lock up early.

courses.name: Cummings Cove Golf & Country Club
courses.summary: Golf Digest 'Best Renovation of Year' 2006. Robert Cupp design plays 3-4 strokes harder than yardage implies. One par-3 tees from a cliff with a 60-foot drop to the green.
courses.insider_tip: Mid-week only for outside access. Back nine plays two full clubs heavier than the yardage book.

courses.name: The Omni Grove Park Inn Course
courses.summary: Donald Ross 1926 redesign, restored to original specs in 2002. The most historically significant resort course in the Southeast — Bobby Jones, Snead, Hogan, Nicklaus, and U.S. presidents have all played here.
courses.insider_tip: No driving range on property. Use the resort's chipping and putting greens to dial in before your round.

courses.name: Waynesville Inn & Golf Club
courses.summary: 27 holes including Donald Ross's original 1926 Carolina nine. Bobby Weed's 2023 renovation produced a best-18 with Slope 139 — deceptively demanding for a mountain resort.
courses.insider_tip: Request the Carolina/Blue Ridge combo. Back three of the Carolina nine play into a brutal afternoon headwind.

courses.name: Maggie Valley Club & Resort
courses.summary: Tucked between Plott Balsam and Great Balsam ranges at 3,400 feet. Every back-nine hole features a mountain ridgeline backdrop. The par-4 10th is 80 feet uphill with a creek at the dogleg.
courses.insider_tip: Book early AM — afternoon cloud and wind from the Tennessee border degrades conditions fast.

courses.name: Springdale Resort
courses.summary: Ron Garl's 2018 renovation restored the 1968 Holmes design — 1,500+ feet of elevation change, Cold Mountain views, creek crossings on multiple holes. Hole 4 ('The Springdale Spasm') is legendary.
courses.insider_tip: Prevailing NW wind adds a full club of headwind on holes 12–15. One of WNC's most underrated public tests.

courses.name: The Cliffs at Walnut Cove
courses.summary: The only Jack Nicklaus Signature Design in WNC — debuted in tournament-ready condition, which is essentially unheard of. One Cliffs membership unlocks all seven network courses.
courses.insider_tip: Confirm guest access well in advance — this property restricts outside play more tightly than other Cliffs courses.

courses.name: The Cliffs at Valley Farms
courses.summary: The second Cliffs community course in the Basin — member-focused companion to Walnut Cove. Single network membership covers all seven Cliffs courses across WNC and the SC Upstate.
courses.insider_tip: Contact Cliffs Living directly for seasonal guest access policies.

courses.name: Biltmore Forest Country Club
courses.summary: Donald Ross 1922. Platinum Clubs of America (top 3% nationally). $2.5M restoration returned original green contours. Access strictly by invitation — this one you earn through connections.
courses.insider_tip: Inverted-saucer Ross greens shed everything that doesn't hold the correct quadrant.

courses.name: Country Club of Asheville
courses.summary: WNC's oldest active private club, roots to 1896. Ross 1928, restored 2016 by Rich Mandell. Climbs Sunset Mountain with sequences of uphill second shots into fast downhill greens.
courses.insider_tip: Club selection from the tee is as important as from the fairway — this vertical track demands it.

courses.name: Champion Hills Club
courses.summary: Tom Fazio 1991 — Golf Digest #1 year-round course in WNC. 350 feet of elevation change through valley corridors producing level lies. Top 30 Best in State 2025-26.
courses.insider_tip: Par-3s can swing 40 yards in effective yardage due to dramatic downhill drops. Trust your eyes.

courses.name: Kenmure Golf Club
courses.summary: Joe Lee 1982, in historic Flat Rock ('Little Charleston of the Mountains'). Notable for walkability and forgiving design philosophy — strategic bunkering rewards course management over power.
courses.insider_tip: Hosts NC state amateur qualifiers — plays longer than yardage suggests due to the Flat Rock plateau elevation.

courses.name: Laurel Ridge Country Club
courses.summary: Bob Cupp 1986 — hosted 50+ national and international tournaments. Slope 146 means business. Outside access available — call ahead. A yardage book is essential on a first visit.
courses.insider_tip: Small, undulating greens reward players who've played the course before. Invest in a yardage book.

courses.name: Boone Golf Club
courses.summary: Ellis Maples 1959 at 3,346 feet — most popular public course in the NC High Country. Golf Digest 4.5 stars. Wide fairways, large undulating bentgrass greens. Book weeks ahead in peak season.
courses.insider_tip: Weekend morning slots fill weeks out May-October. Mid-week early AM is your best shot.

courses.name: Mountain Glen Golf Club
courses.summary: George Cobb 1963 — first public 18-hole course built in the NC High Country. Gentle meadow front nine tightens into strategic woodland back nine. Rarely exceeds 85°F even in August.
courses.insider_tip: July-August tee times here are a premium escape when valley courses are sweltering.

courses.name: Mountain Aire Golf Course
courses.summary: Ashe County gem since 1952 — 30 min from Boone, deliberately removed from the resort scene. One par-3 produces the sensation of 'hitting off the edge of the world' from an elevated tee.
courses.insider_tip: Weekday morning rounds offer fastest pace and peak mountain light on the fairways.

courses.name: Mount Mitchell Golf Club
courses.summary: Fred Hawtree's only U.S. design — the only American work by a British Open rota architect. South Toe River in play on multiple holes. Currently closed post-Helene; monitor for reopening.
courses.insider_tip: At altitude, irons travel 8-12% farther than sea level. Recalibrate every club.

courses.name: Grassy Creek Country Club
courses.summary: Off-the-beaten-path Mitchell County course in the South Toe River corridor. Dramatically undulating terrain, genuine Blue Ridge backdrop. Call ahead — locally operated with limited online presence.
courses.insider_tip: Always call to confirm hours and conditions before making the mountain drive.

courses.name: Linville Falls Golf Club
courses.summary: Casual Parkway-corridor layout near Linville Falls and the Blue Ridge Parkway. Practical public option for Parkway travelers wanting a round without resort pricing.
courses.insider_tip: Confirm hours before visiting — irregular outside peak season.

courses.name: Sugar Mountain Golf Course
courses.summary: The highest publicly accessible golf in the High Country — nearly 5,000 feet elevation. Executive par-64 layout on Sugar Mountain resort. Open April-October. Best value play in the region.
courses.insider_tip: Local residents of Avery, Ashe, Watauga, Mitchell counties get a heavily discounted annual pass.

courses.name: Stone Mountain Golf Club
courses.summary: Adjacent to Stone Mountain State Park — the stone dome face is visible from multiple holes, giving this affordable layout an otherworldly visual backdrop that no landscaping budget could buy.
courses.insider_tip: Pair with a hike in Stone Mountain State Park for an ideal WNC day trip.

courses.name: New River Country Club
courses.summary: Relaxed Alleghany County public course near the Virginia border — distinctly different character from the ski-resort-adjacent High Country courses. Low-pressure, scenic round for families.
courses.insider_tip: Verify hours via GolfNow before visiting — web presence is inconsistently maintained.

courses.name: Rock Creek Country Club
courses.summary: Semi-private Wilkes County club in the foothills transition zone between High Country and the Piedmont. Member-priority with outside tee times at reasonable rates.
courses.insider_tip: Call the pro shop directly for current outside access policies.

courses.name: Country Side Golf Course
courses.summary: Yadkin Valley corridor semi-private in the Elkin/Wilkes foothills. A community staple east of the High Country proper serving the foothills golf market.
courses.insider_tip: Call ahead for current tee time availability for non-members.

courses.name: Forest Pines Golf Course
courses.summary: Second Elkin-area semi-private option — tree-lined Yadkin Valley layout for the foothills market where public options are limited.
courses.insider_tip: Call ahead for current hours and green fees.

courses.name: Linville Golf Club
courses.summary: Donald Ross 1928 near the base of Grandfather Mountain — one of his most remote and dramatic American commissions. The rawness and verticality of this Ross is absent from all his piedmont designs.
courses.insider_tip: Access via Linville Land Harbor lodging packages. Confirm policies with the pro shop — they vary.

courses.name: Olde Beau Resort & Golf Club
courses.summary: NBC GolfPass top-10 in NC. Golfweek Top-50 Development Courses in the Southeast. Renovations eliminated blind shots while preserving dramatic elevation challenges. The 15th and 18th are among the most photographed holes in the Carolinas.
courses.insider_tip: The clubhouse restaurant draws visitors from Charlotte and Raleigh on summer weekends — build in extra time.

courses.name: Jefferson Landing Golf Club
courses.summary: Larry Nelson (2x major champ) 1991 design along the New River — renovated 2019 with Scottish sod-wall bunkers. River in play on six holes. 32,000 sq ft clubhouse with full resort amenities.
courses.insider_tip: Stay-and-play packages through the gated community lodging are excellent value.

courses.name: Linville Ridge Golf Club
courses.summary: Private residential club atop Linville Ridge at 4,500 feet — among the highest private courses in the Southeast. Summer temps rarely reach the low 70s. Altitude adds 12-15% to iron distance.
courses.insider_tip: Recalibrate every club — altitude bonus is real and consistent at this elevation.

courses.name: Elk River Club
courses.summary: First Jack Nicklaus Signature Course in North Carolina (1984). Welcoming river-valley front nine flips to a back nine with water hazards on 8 of 9 holes. Fly-in community with private airstrip.
courses.insider_tip: Birdie on the front; survive the back. The split personality is by Nicklaus's deliberate design.

courses.name: Hound Ears Club
courses.summary: George Cobb 1964 — the High Country's original private golf community. Family-oriented, unpretentious, casual. NC Golf Panel #8 Western region 2021. Local knowledge is a genuine advantage.
courses.insider_tip: Elevation-adjusted distances and predictable valley wind channels reward course familiarity.

courses.name: Blowing Rock Country Club
courses.summary: Storied private club in WNC's most charming summer village. Blue Ridge escarpment views from multiple holes. Tight-knit seasonal member culture — access is about connections, not booking.
courses.insider_tip: Guest access is personal introduction only — the Blowing Rock social scene is the gateway.

courses.name: Grandfather Golf & Country Club
courses.summary: #1 private course in WNC, #2 in NC overall (2026 NC Golf Panel). Ellis Maples 1968, refined by Dan Maples and Bobby Weed. Arnold Palmer called it 'unequalled in North Carolina' for setting. Slope 148.
courses.insider_tip: Two courses on property — use the executive Mountain Springs to warm up before the championship layout.

courses.name: Mountain Air Country Club
courses.summary: One of the Eastern US's only true fly-in golf communities — private airstrip at 5,000+ feet. Members literally fly in to play and fly home. Summer temps rarely exceed 75°F.
courses.insider_tip: Altitude is so significant here that weather patterns can shift in minutes. Be ready for anything.

courses.name: Beech Mountain Club
courses.summary: Willard Byrd 1969, extended by Tom Jackson — plays atop one of the highest incorporated towns in Eastern America, nearly a mile above sea level. Views into Tennessee and Virginia from elevated tees.
courses.insider_tip: Non-members: book a qualifying Beech Mountain lodging rental to unlock guest privileges. Open May-October only.

courses.name: Smoky Mountain Country Club
courses.summary: Literally climbs from valley floor to mountaintop — mid-round vistas of Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Genuine cardiovascular challenge for walkers. Best public-access mountain golf value in the Smokies.
courses.insider_tip: Factor elevation drop AND wind channel into every club selection. Both matter on every hole.

courses.name: Smoky Mountain Golf Club
courses.summary: Haywood County public option complementing the Waynesville Inn resort — more casual, accessible, and affordable. Confirm current status before visiting.
courses.insider_tip: Call ahead — operational status and hours are inconsistently maintained online.

courses.name: Chatuge Shores Golf Course
courses.summary: Lake Chatuge peninsula layout since 1971 — lake visible from multiple fairways with Blue Ridge backdrop. Flat to gently rolling. Check recent reviews for green conditions before booking.
courses.insider_tip: Read recent course reviews carefully — green maintenance has been variable in recent years.

courses.name: Franklin Golf Course
courses.summary: Macon County's primary public golf option. Municipal-style layout in a pleasant mountain setting — prioritizes accessibility and affordability over championship challenge.
courses.insider_tip: Ideal for families and casual golfers visiting the Franklin gem mining corridor.

courses.name: Red Bird Golf Links
courses.summary: Rural public course in Cherokee County — one of the few accessible options near the Georgia and Tennessee borders in far western WNC.
courses.insider_tip: Confirm operational status directly — remote rural facilities in this corridor have limited online presence.

courses.name: ForeU Golf (Brevard)
courses.summary: Modern public facility in Transylvania County — Brevard's 'Land of Waterfalls' market. Accessible, fun experience for all levels near Pisgah National Forest.
courses.insider_tip: Check the website for current format and any technology-enhanced practice features.

courses.name: Mountain Harbour Golf Club
courses.summary: Semi-private on Lake Chatuge in Clay County — lakefront golf with a relaxed community atmosphere. Outside tee times available during off-peak hours.
courses.insider_tip: Call the pro shop for current outside visitor access and available windows.

courses.name: Mill Creek Country Club
courses.summary: Semi-private Franklin corridor option for golfers seeking a membership-oriented experience. Outside play available — confirm with the pro shop before booking.
courses.insider_tip: Call ahead for access policies and current conditions.

courses.name: Sequoyah National Golf Club
courses.summary: Robert Trent Jones II 2009 on Eastern Band Cherokee land — the most awarded public-access mountain course in WNC. Golfweek Top-50 casino courses. Tee shots drop hundreds of feet. Smoky Mountain NP backdrop on every hole.
courses.insider_tip: Pair with a Harrah's Cherokee Casino Resort stay 10 min away for the ultimate WNC golf-and-gaming getaway.

courses.name: Bear Lake Reserve
courses.summary: Private resort community in the Tuckasegee corridor offering lakefront golf as part of a broader lake-and-mountain lifestyle package.
courses.insider_tip: Contact directly for resort guest access rates and tee time availability.

courses.name: High Hampton Resort
courses.summary: Bryan Fazio renovation reopened 2021 — six new holes, bentgrass tee-to-green. National Register property on the historic Hampton estate. Slope 140 now reflects a genuine championship experience.
courses.insider_tip: Golf access has evolved post-2017 ownership change — confirm current resort guest policies directly.

courses.name: Old Edwards Club
courses.summary: Part of the acclaimed Old Edwards Inn — one of the finest boutique hotels in the Southern Appalachians. Resort elegance meets private club service on the Highlands plateau.
courses.insider_tip: Confirm current access procedures and green fees through the resort directly.

courses.name: Balsam Mountain Preserve
courses.summary: Arnold Palmer called it 'different from any course I have ever designed.' Golf Digest Best in State. Elevations to 5,400 feet — the highest Palmer ever worked on in the Eastern US. Slope 149.
courses.insider_tip: When Palmer said 'bring your camera,' he was not being modest. Every forced carry has a view.

courses.name: Wade Hampton Golf Club
courses.summary: Tom Fazio 1987 — Golf Digest Top 100 in the US, top-3 private in NC. Built without a single stick of dynamite, routed entirely through natural valley corridors. Evokes the great inland links of Scotland.
courses.insider_tip: Guest access requires personal member introduction of standing. This one takes a real connection.

courses.name: Mountaintop Golf and Lake Club
courses.summary: Tom Fazio — $1M per hole, blasted from solid rock. Six holes cross a gorge cut by Hurricane Creek. Opening tee drops 100 feet. Golf Digest: 'proof that no property is too rugged for Tom Fazio.'
courses.insider_tip: The par-5 16th is widely cited as one of Fazio's greatest individual holes anywhere in his portfolio.

courses.name: Cullasaja Club
courses.summary: Arnold Palmer 1989 on the Highlands plateau. $3M recent renovation. 350 family members return each summer to what the club calls 'simply the perfect life.' Active golf culture, not just an amenity.
courses.insider_tip: The club explicitly acknowledges it 'may not be for everyone.' Casual elegance is the operating ethos.

courses.name: Highlands Country Club
courses.summary: The oldest private club in Highlands (1928) — social heart of the summer colony for nearly a century. Ron Pritchard design emphasizes position and short-game skill over power.
courses.insider_tip: Member privacy is paramount here. Proper introduction is the only path in.

courses.name: Highlands Falls Country Club
courses.summary: George Cobb 1962, updated by Joe Lee in the 1980s — the most accessible of the Highlands private courses in terms of slope difficulty. Mountain views on multiple holes.
courses.insider_tip: Access through member accompaniment — a welcoming option for first-time Highlands visitors.

courses.name: Wildcat Cliffs Country Club
courses.summary: George Cobb 1961 with sweeping views of the Blue Ridge and Whiteside Mountain corridor. The community is named for the dramatic granite cliffs visible from upper course holes.
courses.insider_tip: Some of the most sought-after private real estate in the Highlands market surrounds this course.

courses.name: The Country Club of Sapphire Valley
courses.summary: Golf centerpiece of one of the most established private residential communities in the Cashiers/Sapphire corridor. Plays through terrain above Lake Sapphire on the high Cashiers plateau.
courses.insider_tip: Contact the club for current member access policies.

courses.name: Burlingame Country Club
courses.summary: Private lakefront country club in the Sapphire Valley of Transylvania County — mountain golf with direct lake access in one of the most beautiful private communities in the Cashiers corridor.
courses.insider_tip: Golf is a central but not exclusive amenity — the full community lifestyle is the draw.

courses.name: Trillium Links & Lake Club
courses.summary: Morris Hatalsky 1998 within the Trillium residential community — community-focused social golf complemented by boating on the adjacent lake. Understated alternative to nearby headline courses.
courses.insider_tip: Access through membership and accompaniment — a relaxed, social atmosphere defines the experience.

courses.name: Lake Lure Municipal Golf Course
courses.summary: Donald Ross 1927, 9-hole municipal — Chimney Rock ridgeline views, nearly a century of intact routing. The Great Depression prevented the planned second nine from ever being built.
courses.insider_tip: Excellent pre- or post-round option when visiting Lake Lure's water recreation offerings.

courses.name: Silver Creek Golf Club
courses.summary: Value-oriented Burke County public course in the foothills transition zone between the Blue Ridge and the NC Piedmont. Open, rolling character.
courses.insider_tip: Confirm current conditions and hours directly with the pro shop before visiting.

courses.name: Meadowbrook Golf Club
courses.summary: Accessible, affordable public golf in Rutherford County's broad valley terrain. Open pastoral character — comfortable for beginners and recreational golfers.
courses.insider_tip: Verify current green fees directly with the pro shop.

courses.name: Quaker Meadows Golf Club
courses.summary: Historically significant Burke County grounds — site of a Cherokee settlement and the Overmountain Men muster in the Revolution. Golf layered onto land with more backstory than almost any course in WNC.
courses.insider_tip: The most historically rich grounds of any public course in WNC. Look up the Overmountain Men before you play.

courses.name: Lenoir Golf Course
courses.summary: Caldwell County's primary municipal public option in the easternmost WNC foothills. Accessible public golf at municipal pricing.
courses.insider_tip: Confirm current hours and conditions through the city parks and recreation department.

courses.name: Forest City Municipal Golf Course
courses.summary: 9-hole Rutherford County municipal — entry-level pricing, easy-walking flat terrain in the Broad River Valley. Solid casual afternoon option near Chimney Rock and Lake Lure.
courses.insider_tip: Good warmup round before tackling the more demanding Rumbling Bald or Cleghorn.

courses.name: Dogwood Valley Golf Course
courses.summary: Well-regarded Caroleen/Forest City local public track — consistently positive regional reviews for condition and value. Tree-lined foothills corridor, a step up from the municipal layouts.
courses.insider_tip: One of the better-maintained budget public options in Rutherford County.

courses.name: Rutherfordton Golf Club
courses.summary: Community public course in the Rutherford County seat. Casual, local atmosphere in rolling foothills terrain.
courses.insider_tip: Verify current operational status before visiting — online info is inconsistently maintained.

courses.name: Orchard Trace Golf Club
courses.summary: WNC's most distinctive par-3 course on former apple orchard land — each hole named for an apple variety. The ONLY fully lighted course in WNC, open until 1:30 AM seven days a week.
courses.insider_tip: Perfect for twilight rounds after dinner in downtown Hendersonville — the evening rates are a steal.

courses.name: Cleghorn Golf & Sports Club
courses.summary: George Cobb 1972 (Augusta Par-3 Course, Quail Hollow architect) — Golf Digest 'Best Places to Play.' The 1837 manor house is visible from the fairways. Adjacent to Tryon International Equestrian Center.
courses.insider_tip: Course record 61 by Dave Long Jr. — conditions are maintained to a high standard for a public-access track.

courses.name: Rumbling Bald — Apple Valley
courses.summary: Dan Maples 1986 — Golf Digest praised it as one of the most beautiful mountain courses in the region. 75% of shots are level or downhill (nearly impossible on a mountain layout). Bald Mountain rock face looms above the final holes.
courses.insider_tip: Aggressive play is consistently rewarded here. The layout is literally designed for it.

courses.name: Rumbling Bald — Bald Mountain
courses.summary: W.B. Lewis 1973 — tight corridors pressing against the granite cliffs of Bald Mountain. The par-3 12th plays directly against an exposed cliff face. Best 36-hole foothills combo paired with Apple Valley.
courses.insider_tip: Play both Rumbling Bald courses in a single day for the most varied foothills golf experience in WNC.

courses.name: Red Fox Country Club
courses.summary: Ellis Maples 1968 hidden gem — 7,104 yards, rating 74.5, slope 136. Championship-caliber layout available as semi-private at modest rates. In the heart of Tryon's equestrian corridor.
courses.insider_tip: One of WNC's best-kept secrets for value. Plays like a private club, priced like a public course.

courses.name: Silver Creek Plantation
courses.summary: Private gated residential community in Burke County with golf as a central amenity, serving the Morganton private club market.
courses.insider_tip: Contact the membership office for access policies and specifications.

courses.name: Mimosa Hills Golf & Country Club
courses.summary: Donald Ross 1929 restored by Kris Spence — NC Golf Panel #10 Western region 2026. U.S. Open Sectional Qualifying host. Holes routed to maximize Blue Ridge Mountain panoramas.
courses.insider_tip: Invitation-only access from an existing member. Among the most important private memberships in the eastern WNC foothills.

courses.name: Tryon Country Club
courses.summary: Oldest golf course in Polk County — laid out 1914, attributed to Donald Ross. The 1922 Rustic Revival log clubhouse is a National Register property. A course for golf history enthusiasts.
courses.insider_tip: The entire 90-acre grounds are a remarkably intact example of early-20th-century mountain golf culture.

courses.name: Bright's Creek Golf Club
courses.summary: Tom Fazio 2006 — one of his personal favorites. Golf Digest top-37 in the nation. 4,700-acre private estate at the thermal belt foot of the Blue Ridge. Civil War-era cemeteries preserved within the course boundaries.
courses.insider_tip: Discovery weekend packages available for serious membership prospects — the only non-member path in.
